title: Aeropuerto Arturo Merino Benítez 15 — FINAL v2
location: Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport (SCL), Santiago, Chile — LATAM Luggage Service Counter
classification: Attorney Work Product — Privileged and Confidential

cluster_A_opening_challenge.summary: Passenger opens with direct challenge: names three harms (removal, physical mistreatment, use of force), characterizes removal justification as 'una mentira', invokes camera evidence, offers to leave voluntarily if proven wrong.
cluster_A_opening_challenge.reasoning: Leandro opens by framing three harms: removal from flight, physical mistreatment ('me machucaron'), and use of force. He immediately characterizes the removal justification as 'una mentira' (a lie) — the false aggression allegation — and invokes camera evidence with an offer to leave voluntarily if the allegation is proven. This is consistent with F-002 (assertive but not aggressive, conditional resolution) and directly corroborates F-003 (the false-aggression-allegation narrative explicitly challenged on tape). Dominika's initial response defers: 'Eso se lo explicaron en el proceso'.

cluster_B_shifting_narratives.summary: Passenger exposes LATAM's shifting justifications: first narrative = aggression, after cameras disproved → second narrative = 'pasó solito su Boarding Pass'. The same person who handed him his boarding pass is the one who falsely accused him.
cluster_B_shifting_narratives.reasoning: This cluster captures the shifting-narrative pattern documented in F-003 and F-004. First narrative: 'aggression' against a crew member. After cameras disproved it → second narrative: 'he passed his own boarding pass' (procedural violation). Leandro additionally identifies that the same person who handed him his boarding pass is the one who falsely accused him — a conflict-of-interest/self-serving accusation dynamic. In seg 15, Leandro reports overhearing LATAM staff say they need 'una carta comprobando exactamente por qué sacaron' because 'ellos quieren sacar su responsabilidad' — revealing LATAM's internal concern about liability and need for post-hoc justification.
cluster_B_shifting_narratives.violation_linkage: Supports F-003 (manufactured pretext — shifting narratives) and F-004 (post-hoc justification).

cluster_C_cellphone_document.summary: Critical evidentiary detail: LATAM generated the removal-justification document but refused to print it. Document existed only on Joaquín Barraza's personal cellphone when shown to PDI. Demonstrates avoidance of durable written record.
cluster_C_cellphone_document.reasoning: This is a critical new evidentiary detail. Leandro identifies that the removal document ('la carta') was made by LATAM — directly contradicting later staff claims that documentation comes from PDI. Dominika confirms she spoke with Joaquín Barraza. Leandro states LATAM 'ni siquiera... quiso como imprimir' the document and instead sent Barraza to PDI with the document only on his phone. This demonstrates informality/irregularity in the documentation process, supporting the inference that LATAM avoided creating a durable written record of its own removal justification — consistent with the documentation-refusal pattern (F-005) and internal-channel capture (F-016).
provisions_engaged: LPDC Art. 3(e) (undue delays in provision of information)
CACH Art. 133 (obligation to provide written reasons)
cluster_C_cellphone_document.violation_linkage: Supports F-005 expanded (documentation-refusal arc) and F-016 (internal-channel capture).

cluster_D_documentation_demand.summary: Passenger demands written documentation; Dominika refuses and threatens second forced removal from luggage area ('Tenemos y debemos sacarlo de este lugar'). Conditional cooperation offered only if passenger leaves.
cluster_D_documentation_demand.reasoning: Leandro articulates a clear need for written documentation to rebook travel and preserve evidence. Dominika deflects jurisdiction to PDI/Seguridad Aeroportuaria, ignoring that the document was generated by LATAM. She then escalates to a removal threat: 'Este es un espacio privado. Si yo le pido que salga usted, debe salir. Tenemos y debemos sacarlo de este lugar.' This is the second LATAM removal threat of the day (first from the aircraft, now from luggage counter), establishing a pattern of removal as the default response to documentation requests. The subsequent 'amable' advice to file a PDI complaint is offered as an alternative to LATAM providing its own documentation.
provisions_engaged: Art. 23 bis (burden of proof on provider)
Art. 50 (unfair contract terms — removal for requesting documentation)
CACH Art. 133B (right to written statement of reasons)
cluster_D_documentation_demand.violation_linkage: F-005 expanded — documentation refusal now includes a second removal threat. New finding candidate: second-area removal threat.

cluster_E_national_origin.summary: Dominika invokes passenger's country of origin ('su país de origen') in procedural justification. When directly asked about removal procedures, admits 'No lo sé, no lo sé por qué son así'.
cluster_E_national_origin.reasoning: Leandro asserts prior airport work experience. Dominika responds by introducing a national-origin distinction: 'los procedimientos que pueden aplicar acá pueden ser muy diferentes a los de su país de origen.' Nationality was irrelevant to the documentation question. The implication is that the passenger's expectations are foreign and inapplicable, aligning with the broader pattern (STG_13 seg 15: 'cuál es tu cultura'). While this single exchange does not independently establish discriminatory intent, it is a corroborating data point for the discrimination-on-nationality finding candidate. Additionally, Dominika's admission 'No lo sé, no lo sé por qué son así' reveals procedural opacity from a supervisor.
provisions_engaged: CONST Art. 19 N°2 (equality, no arbitrary discrimination)
cluster_E_national_origin.violation_linkage: Supports pending discrimination-on-nationality finding; cross-reference STG_13 seg 15.

cluster_F_final_standoff.summary: Passenger describes feeling like 'pelota de ping-pong', makes closing summary: at airport since 11am, should be at final destination, blocked by proven false accusation. Dominika makes assistance conditional on departure.
cluster_F_final_standoff.reasoning: Leandro uses the 'pelota de ping-pong' metaphor for being bounced between departments, echoing the same phrase later in STG_3. Dominika cannot explain removal procedures ('No lo sé por qué son así') and makes assistance conditional on the passenger leaving the area, creating a catch-22: leaving means losing the document trail, staying means being threatened with removal. Leandro's closing summary (seg 89) articulates the full harm arc: at the airport since 11 AM, should be at final destination, blocked by a lie 'ya fue comprobada por la policía.' His distress is consistent with F-002's bearing — distress, not aggression.
provisions_engaged: CACH Art. 133A (carrier duties to stranded passengers)
